2026-12-14.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Apparition to St Joseph · St John of the Cross
readings: Carry the cross and count the cost
2026-12-14.alt: St John of the Cross, Carmelite friar and mystic (died 1591), Doctor of the Church; Mar Abraham Kidunaya, Syrian hermit (Tradition). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-14.verse: Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
theo: Hebrews meditates on a mysterious figure: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham and received a tenth of everything. His name means “king of righteousness” and Salem means “peace”. With no recorded father or mother, no beginning or end, “resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.” Genesis says he brought out bread and wine; the Fathers saw in him a sign of Christ, the eternal Priest who offers himself under bread and wine.

Jesus turns to the crowds following him and tells them the cost of discipleship: to put him before every family tie, even before one's own life; to carry the cross; to sit down and count the cost like a builder or a king going to war. “None of you can become my disciple if you do not give up all your possessions.” St John of the Cross lived this in the dark night of prison and wrote some of the most beautiful poetry of love for God. The way of the cross leads to the light of Christmas and of Easter.
outline: What does following Jesus cost you?
“Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
live: Bear one difficulty today without complaining, for love of Christ.
Complete one good resolution you made at the start of the fast.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Priest after the order of Melchizedek, give us courage to carry our cross and follow you, and through the prayers of St John of the Cross, lead us through every dark night into your light. Amen.
altar: Christ, priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, offers himself to the Father under the signs of bread and wine, and gives himself to us.

quick: Melchizedek, priest of bread and wine, points to Christ.
Count the cost and finish the work.

2026-12-14.question: What cross am I avoiding?

family.explain: Jesus wants to be first in our lives, even before family and friends. Following Jesus is worth everything.
family.intention: We pray for those who give up much to follow Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we put Jesus first in our family?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, eternal High Priest, you call us to follow you with all our heart. As we gather, help us to count the cost and choose you. Amen.
share: Jesus says whoever does not carry the cross cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:27). What cross am I avoiding?
What do I put before Jesus?
How has God blessed me when I put him first?
pm.resp: Lord, you are first in our lives.
interc: For priests, that they may be faithful to Christ the eternal High Priest.
For those who leave everything to follow Christ.
For contemplatives, through the prayers of St John of the Cross.
For those who are afraid of the cost of discipleship.
For our families, that Jesus may be first in our homes.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son is priest for ever. Give us courage to put him first, to carry our cross and to follow him with all our hearts. Amen.

illus: A young doctor from Kerala was offered a well-paid post in the US, but felt called to work in a mission hospital in Jharkhand. Her parents were upset. She said: “I counted the cost. Jesus is worth it.” Years later her parents visit her hospital every Christmas.

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews speaks of Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who met Abraham and blessed him, and to whom Abraham gave a tenth of everything (Hebrews 7:1–2). Melchizedek appears without genealogy, a mysterious figure resembling the Son of God, a priest for ever (Hebrews 7:3).
Melchizedek offered bread and wine (Genesis 14:18). The Church sees in him a figure of Christ, the eternal High Priest, who offers himself under the signs of bread and wine in the Holy Qurbono.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks hard words to the crowds who follow him: whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and even life itself, cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:26–27).

Hate here is a Semitic way of saying: love less than me. Jesus must come first. Then he gives two examples: a man building a tower first sits down to estimate the cost; a king going to war first considers whether he can win (Luke 14:28–32). Discipleship must be chosen with open eyes.
Today we also remember St John of the Cross, who counted the cost and gave everything for God, finding in the dark night the light of divine love.

During this fast, let us count the cost of following Jesus and choose him again. What do I put before him: family, money, comfort, reputation? Let us give him the first place, so that at Yaldo he may be born in a heart that belongs to him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus carried His cross because He loves us. When something is hard, offer it to Jesus with love!

intro: Theme: “Carry the cross and follow me.”
The eternal Priest and the cost of discipleship.

sub: He resembles the Son of God, a priest forever.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
points.apply: Receive Holy Communion this week with special attention.

sub: The psalmist lifts the cup in thanks.
q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me? I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD,
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Bear one difficulty today without complaining.

sub: By wisdom a house is built.
q: By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established;
For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not first sit down and estimate the cost, to see whether he has enough to complete it?

concl: Christ the eternal Priest goes before us with his cross.
Let us follow to the end.
